1.Nf3 Nf6 2.b3 d5 3.Bb2.strategy: Completes the queenside fianchetto: the bishop looks down the long diagonal at f6 and the kingside, while the b3 pawn covers c4. White lets Black hold a pawn in the centre and plans to undermine it from a distance rather than occupy it, keeping the choice of pawn break for later.

1.Nf3 Nf6 2.b3 d5 3.Bb2 c5.strategy: Strikes at d4 straight away, claiming queenside space and making a central advance hard for White. Black builds a pawn centre on d5 and c5 that White will try to undermine with piece pressure, so the game turns on whether that centre proves a strength or a target.

1.Nf3 Nf6 2.b3 d5 3.Bb2 g6.strategy: Mirrors White's set-up: the fianchettoed bishop will oppose the bishop on b2 along the long diagonal, while the d5 pawn holds the centre. Black chooses a solid, evenly balanced game over grabbing queenside space and keeps the c-pawn flexible.
